mainEntity.name: Does a healing cap hurt to have fitted?

acceptedAnswer.text: The fitting of a healing cap is generally a minor procedure and is not typically painful. It is usually carried out under local anaesthesia or at a point when the area is already numb following implant surgery. After the anaesthetic wears off, some tenderness or mild discomfort around the site is normal for a few days and can usually be managed with over-the-counter pain relief as recommended by your dentist. If pain persists beyond a few days or worsens, contact your dental practice for advice.

mainEntity.name: How long does a healing cap stay in place?

acceptedAnswer.text: The length of time a healing cap remains in place varies between patients and depends on how well the implant is integrating with the bone and how the soft tissue is healing. For many patients, this phase lasts between four and twelve weeks, though it can be longer in some cases. Your dentist will assess progress at review appointments and advise when it is appropriate to move to the next stage of treatment.

mainEntity.name: Can I eat normally with a healing cap?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most patients can eat comfortably during the healing period, though it is generally advisable to be cautious near the implant site. Avoiding very hard, sticky, or chewy foods directly on the healing cap reduces the risk of disturbing the site or dislodging the component. Your dental team will provide specific dietary guidance based on your individual circumstances and the location of the implant in your mouth.

mainEntity.name: What happens if my healing cap comes loose?

acceptedAnswer.text: A healing cap should remain securely in place during the healing phase. If you notice that it feels loose or has come out, contact your dental practice as soon as possible. This does not necessarily indicate a serious problem, but the cap should be re-examined and re-secured by your dentist to prevent the gum tissue from healing in an unguided way. Avoid attempting to reposition it yourself.

mainEntity.name: Is a healing cap always necessary with dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not all implant treatment pathways involve a distinct healing cap stage. Some approaches, such as immediate loading protocols, may follow a different sequence. Whether a healing cap is part of your treatment plan depends on your individual clinical situation, the type of implant system used, and your dentist's assessment of the most appropriate approach. Your dental team will explain each stage of your specific treatment plan before it begins.

mainEntity.name: Can a healing cap affect the appearance of my smile?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because the healing cap sits at or just above the gumline, it may be briefly visible if the implant is in a prominent position. However, it is a temporary component and is only present during the healing phase. Your dentist can discuss what to expect at each stage, including how the healing cap will look and how it will be replaced with a natural-looking final crown once healing is complete.
